description: IR mode active. Empty main entrance gate. A stray cat moves along the perimeter wall near the gate post. No personnel present. Ambient temperature low; slight fog visible on lens edges.
Parking lot B fully vacant. Overhead sodium lamp flickering on the eastern row. No vehicles or pedestrians detected. Motion trigger was a piece of plastic bag carried by wind across sensor zone.

IR mode. Single male figure observed walking slowly along the outer fence line on the north side. Subject pauses near junction post, looks around, then continues walking east. Security patrol dispatched; confirmed as night-shift staff doing a routine perimeter walk.
Loading dock area silent. Cargo truck (partial plate: MH-12-**-4421) parked in authorized bay 3 from previous evening. No activity detected. Dock lights on standby mode.
Rooftop camera. Clear sky, minimal cloud cover. No personnel on roof. All rooftop HVAC units operational. No anomalies detected.
South corridor internal camera. Cleaning staff (1 male, yellow vest, ID badge visible) operating floor-buffing machine near fire exit. Motion consistent with regular cleaning schedule. No concerns.

IR mode. Rear service gate. A dark-colored sedan slows down outside the gate, idles for approximately 40 seconds, then drives away without stopping. Partial plate read: KA-05-**. Alert flagged for review. No further activity.
Stairwell B, floor 1. Motion detected. Security guard (female, gray uniform) conducting rounds. Badge scan logged at stairwell door. Proceeding to floor 2. No issues.

Main entrance gate. Single male pedestrian approaches gate on foot, attempts intercom. No response as facility is closed. Subject waits approximately 2 minutes, then walks away south along the road. No access granted.

Parking lot B. A white utility van (plate partially obscured by mud: GJ-**-7843) enters the lot and parks in an unmarked bay near the south hedge. Two occupants remain inside the vehicle. Flagged as unusual activity; security notified.

North fence line. IR camera detects two individuals crouching near fence panel 7. One subject appears to be testing fence tension by pulling on it. Security team alerted immediately. Subjects fled eastward on foot before guards arrived. Incident logged as attempted perimeter breach.
Loading dock. No activity. Dock doors sealed. Truck in bay 3 unchanged. Motion sensor tripped by moth near IR emitter — false positive.
Rooftop camera. Wind picking up; HVAC unit 3 rattling slightly. No personnel detected. Rooftop access hatch confirmed closed by sensor log.
South corridor. Cleaning staff has completed floor 1. Cart now stationary near supply closet. Staff member enters closet, retrieves mop bucket, exits. Routine activity confirmed.
Rear service gate. Security guard (male, heavy-set) performs scheduled gate check. Padlock and chain confirmed intact. Guard signs physical logbook at gate post. Returns to guardhouse via same path.

Stairwell B, floor 2. Smoke detector triggered briefly — possibly dust disturbance from cleaning activities below. Alarm reset within 30 seconds. No fire or smoke visually detected on camera. Maintenance noted.
Main gate. IR mode. A delivery scooter (TN-09-**-2210) approaches gate, presses intercom. Night guard speaks through intercom and informs rider that deliveries begin at 06:00. Rider departs.

Parking lot B. White van from 02:03 is still present. One occupant now visible outside the vehicle, standing near the rear. Second occupant remains inside. No hostile action. Security advised to monitor.
North fence. All clear. No persons or animals detected. Wind causing tree branches to brush fence, generating intermittent motion sensor noise. Sensor sensitivity adjusted remotely by control room.
Loading dock. First early staff member (female, logistics team jacket, carrying thermos) arrives and enters dock office via side personnel door. Badge scan verified. Routine early-shift arrival.
Rooftop at pre-dawn. Faint orange glow on horizon. No personnel. Flock of birds lands on western parapet briefly, then departs. No structural or equipment anomalies.
South corridor. Second cleaning crew member (male, same company uniform) arrives and begins mopping near the emergency exit. Exit door sensor confirms door is closed and locked. No issues.

Rear service gate. A compact grey car parks outside the gate. Driver exits carrying a toolbox and a hi-vis jacket. Waits outside gate, checking phone. Appears to be a contractor waiting for site opening. No unauthorized access attempted.
Stairwell B. Day shift changeover beginning. Guard supervisor (female, white shirt) descends stairwell from floor 3, heading to ground floor briefing room. Badge scan at each floor landing confirmed.

Main entrance gate. Day shift security officer activates gate console. Gate arm raised to open. First vehicle of the day — a silver Toyota Innova (DL-08-**-6677) — enters smoothly after ID check. Occupant: 1 male, appears to be senior management based on reserved parking sticker.
Parking lot B. White van from overnight visit finally departs, reversing out of bay without incident. Guard at gate notes plate for log. Lot otherwise empty.

North fence exterior, dawn. First light. A cyclist (male) passes along the public footpath adjacent to the outer fence. He is riding quickly and does not slow. Normal public activity on adjacent path.
North fence. Daylight now fully established. Groundskeeper (male, green overalls) begins grass-trimming along inner fence line. Normal activity.

Loading dock. First delivery truck of the day arrives — large curtain-sided lorry (MH-12-GH-4421), same vehicle from overnight parking. Driver (male) presents delivery manifest to dock officer. Dock door 2 raised. Unloading begins.

Rooftop. Maintenance technician (male, red hard hat) accesses rooftop via hatch. Carrying tool bag. Conducts visual inspection of HVAC unit 3. Works for approximately 15 minutes. Hatch re-secured on departure.

South corridor. Morning foot traffic picks up. Three staff members badge in through south door within a 4-minute window. All wearing company lanyards. One stops to check notice board. Normal start-of-day behavior.
Rear service gate. Contractor from 05:45 granted access after identity verification. Escort provided by facilities staff (female). Both proceed toward utilities block. Gate re-secured.

Stairwell B. Continuous foot traffic — approximately 14 individuals ascending/descending over a 10-minute window as morning shift begins. All badge access events logged normally. No tailgating detected.

Main gate. Rush-hour pedestrian entry stream begins. Gate guard scanning ID cards manually for visitors. One individual (male, backpack, no lanyard) stopped and redirected to visitor reception. Vehicle queue forming — 6 cars waiting.

Parking lot B. A delivery drone hovers briefly over the parking lot, apparently surveying for a package drop zone. It ascends and departs without landing. Operator contacted by security email. Facility no-fly policy over internal grounds confirmed to operator.
Parking lot B now 40% full. Multiple vehicles arriving in 2-minute intervals. A red hatchback (KA-03-MN-9920) parks across two bays. No personnel intervene immediately. Noted for parking enforcement.

North fence exterior. A male pedestrian (baseball cap, dark tracksuit) stops outside the fence and stares toward the facility buildings for approximately 90 seconds. Takes out phone, appears to photograph the facility through the fence. Moves on after a slow walk east. Flagged for review.

Loading dock. Second delivery vehicle arrives — refrigerated unit (MH-14-**-8832). Driver presents cold-chain documentation. Dock 1 opened. Two dock workers assist with unloading. All wearing appropriate PPE.
Rooftop. Maintenance technician from earlier returns with a second colleague. Both working on HVAC unit 3. Tools spread around work area. Safety harnesses visible. Routine maintenance ongoing.
Rooftop. Early morning. A single seagull lands on rooftop parapet and remains for 12 minutes before flying off. Normal wildlife activity. Camera lens tested — clear, no obstructions.

South corridor. A large group of approximately 8 visitors in lanyards with VISITOR badges move through corridor escorted by a company host (female, blue blazer). Tour group progressing toward conference suite. Normal.

Rear service gate. An unattended brown cardboard package spotted just outside the gate, leaning against the gatepost. No delivery vehicle seen. Security protocol initiated — area cordoned. Package later confirmed as a misdirected courier parcel containing office stationery.

Stairwell B, floor 3. Two male employees engaged in a heated verbal argument near the stairwell entrance. Voices raised, one pointing finger aggressively. A third employee intervenes. Situation de-escalates within 2 minutes. Reported to HR. No physical altercation.

Main gate. A male individual in business attire arrives at gate without a vehicle. He presents a business card rather than a company-issued ID. Guard follows visitor protocol: takes photograph of national ID, issues temporary visitor badge, notifies the internal contact. HR representative arrives at gate in 6 minutes to escort visitor. All documented.

Main gate. Pedestrian flow steady — approximately 3-5 persons entering per 5-minute block. A courier (female, motorcycle helmet still on) presents parcel delivery at gate. Guard directs to reception. Vehicle (KA-09-**) proceeds to visitor bay.

Parking lot B. The red hatchback double-parked from 08:10 now has a parking notice placed on windscreen by facilities staff. Owner approaches from main building, acknowledges the notice, repositions vehicle correctly.

North fence interior. Groundskeeper continues maintenance. Noticed a gap in mesh fencing at panel 9 — approximately 20cm wide, likely caused by vandalism or animal activity. Reports to facilities. Flagged for urgent repair.

Loading dock. During morning unloading, a pallet is accidentally dropped from the tail-lift of the delivery truck, spilling several boxes onto the dock floor. No personnel are hit. Driver and dock crew assess spilled goods. No injuries reported. Goods re-palletized and checked for damage.
Loading dock. Refrigerated truck completes unloading and departs. Bay 1 closed and secured. Dock officer conducts post-delivery inspection of bay area. All pallets counted and logged. Normal.
Rooftop. Maintenance team finishes HVAC unit 3 servicing. Equipment packed up, rooftop left clear. Hatch locked on exit. Both technicians sign out at facilities desk per visitor log.

South corridor. A trolley loaded with IT equipment (monitors, server components) is moved through the corridor by two IT staff members. Equipment is logged on a transfer form visible on the top of the trolley. Normal authorized asset movement.

South corridor. Fire drill alarm activated as a scheduled test. Staff exit calmly and in an orderly manner. Corridor cleared within 2 minutes. Evacuation marshal (male, orange vest) sweeps corridor and confirms empty before following out. All clear confirmed.
Rear service gate. Contractor and escort return from utilities block. Contractor collects equipment and departs via rear gate. Gate re-secured by escort. All documented.
Stairwell B. Normal mid-morning movement. Several individuals using stairs instead of lift — consistent with wellness initiative campaign visible on notice board. No incidents.

Parking lot B. Two young males (no badges, casual clothing) observed climbing over the low decorative wall from the adjacent public plaza into the parking lot periphery. They appear to be teenagers. Guard approaches; they claim they were taking a shortcut. Both escorted back to public area. Pedestrian entry point noted for potential barrier improvement.
Main gate. A taxi (TN-22-**-5510) drops off two suited visitors. Both proceed to reception desk inside gate. Guard logs their arrival. Vehicle departs after a 30-second wait.

Parking lot B. 75% capacity. Staff members walking to and from vehicles during morning break period. A male employee is spotted leaning against a car that does not appear to be his own — he walks away quickly when approached by a colleague. Minor concern noted.

North fence, interior side. A facilities worker is using an angle grinder near the fence for metal-cutting work on a drainage cover. Sparks visible. All PPE in use: face shield, gloves, and ear protection. Hot-work permit confirmed checked by control room.
North fence. Midday. Repair team (2 workers, facilities uniforms) arrives to patch gap at panel 9. They unroll wire mesh and begin repair work. Activity consistent with work order raised at 10:13.

Loading dock. A dock worker reports a fuel smell near bay 2. Area evacuated as a precaution. Facilities finds a small diesel spill from the earlier refrigerated truck — approximately 30cm puddle under the loading lip. Spill kit deployed. Area cleared within 15 minutes. Bay re-opened after air quality check passes.

Loading dock. Third delivery truck of the day (UP-85-**-3301) arrives. Driver argues with dock officer about delivery slot — not pre-scheduled. Officer denies access pending authorization. Driver waits outside in vehicle.

Rooftop. A drone is observed flying slowly above the facility at moderate altitude — appears to be hovering and changing angles as if surveying. Drone not company-owned. Security supervisor notified. Footage saved as evidence. Facility is within a restricted drone zone. Incident escalated to local authority.
Rooftop. Completely clear. Bright midday sun. No personnel or anomalies. All HVAC units operating normally. Camera pan function cycles through full arc — all clear.

South corridor. A staff member (female, finance department lanyard) is seen leaving the corridor fire door propped open with a chair — likely to allow airflow. Fire safety violation. Guard immediately removes the chair and closes the door. Staff member spoken to about fire safety compliance.

South corridor. Lunchtime traffic high. Groups of 3-5 staff members moving through corridor toward canteen wing. All wearing badges. A visitor badge spotted hanging loosely from someone's jacket pocket — guard approaches, confirms it is a valid visitor with host still nearby.

Rear service gate. Gate-mounted intercom triggers without visible person at camera. Guard investigates via PTZ — no one present. Possibly a wind-related contact on the intercom call button. Guard physically checks gate exterior — no one. Logged as equipment false trigger. Intercom button to be inspected by maintenance.

Rear service gate. Delivery driver from unscheduled 12:14 arrival finally granted access after supervisor approval obtained. Driver proceeds to dock bay 3 under escort. Partial plate logged: UP-85-HJ.

Stairwell B, floor 2. An employee in distress (female, sitting on stairwell landing with hands on her face, appears to be crying) is detected. Guard responds within 2 minutes. Employee states she is dealing with personal stress. Guard informs her about the Employee Assistance Program. Wellness team notified (anonymized). No security threat.

Stairwell B, floor 1. A male individual in civilian clothes (no lanyard, no badge) observed entering stairwell behind a badged employee — classic tailgating event. Security alerted. Individual intercepted on floor 2 landing, identified as a vendor representative who forgot their visitor pass at reception. Escorted back to reception.

Main gate. A heated verbal dispute occurs at the gate between a gate guard and a vehicle driver (male, mid-40s) who insists his visitor clearance should have been pre-approved but no record exists. Driver becomes increasingly agitated, honking repeatedly. Supervisor dispatched. Clearance eventually located in email — approved but not entered into system. Access granted after 18-minute delay. Incident flagged for process improvement.

Main gate. A black SUV (HR-26-**-1122) with tinted windows pulls up. Driver presents credentials. After a 3-minute verification hold, access granted. Vehicle directed to VIP bay near main building entrance.

Parking lot B. A group of 3 unknown males (no badges, casual clothes) observed entering the parking lot on foot via the pedestrian cut-through from the road. They appear to be looking at parked vehicles closely. Security personnel intercepted them — confirmed as car dealership representatives looking for a staff member's vehicle with prior consent. Still documented.
North fence. Fence repair at panel 9 completed. Workers remove tools and equipment. Area looks intact. Supervisor (male) inspects the patch and signs off. Workers depart via service road.

Loading dock. A dock worker is observed using a personal mobile phone while operating a manual pallet jack. Phone policy violation logged. Supervisor (male) verbally reminds the worker of the policy. Worker pockets phone and continues with task.

Loading dock. Afternoon shift dock team of 3 workers arrives and relieves morning crew. Brief handover at dock office. Morning crew departs. Dock bay 2 receives a fourth truck — scheduled delivery of packaging materials (MH-04-**-6654). Unloading begins without incident.

Rooftop. Midday. A sudden heavy rain shower begins. Camera rain wiper activates. Visibility slightly reduced but acceptable. All HVAC units remain operational. Roof drainage working correctly — water channeling to downpipes. No standing water.

Rooftop. A female employee in office attire accesses rooftop via hatch — appears to be on a personal phone call, pacing. Non-authorized recreational use of rooftop. Guard dispatched to ask her to return indoors per policy.

South corridor. A delivery of food and beverages on a trolley is pushed through the corridor by a catering company employee (branded uniform, valid visitor pass). Heading to floor 2 meeting room. Catering employee signed in at reception and escorted to floor. Normal.

South corridor. A large crowd of approximately 30 employees gathers near the south corridor fire exit — an informal announcement by a department head about a team milestone. Group disperses after approximately 7 minutes when HR asks them to move to the canteen. Corridor temporarily blocked but resolved.

South corridor. An unattended black laptop bag spotted near bench opposite south door. No owner visible. Security staff isolate the area and broadcast announcement. Owner (female) returns within 90 seconds and collects bag. Owner admonished for leaving it unattended.
Rear service gate. Routine delivery of office supplies by a courier on a bicycle. Rider hands parcel through gate wicket to guard. Parcel logged and moved to mailroom. Gate not opened.

Stairwell B. Afternoon traffic moderate. A fire extinguisher on floor 2 landing appears to have been moved from its bracket and placed on the ground. Guard repositions it and logs the incident for maintenance inspection.

Main gate. A taxi stops outside the gate. Passenger (female, carrying a suitcase) exits and approaches gate intercom. States she is arriving for a scheduled interview. Guard verifies against interview list — name confirmed. Visitor badge issued. Taxi departs.

Main gate. A school bus (repurposed, no commercial plate) attempts entry claiming to carry a tour group. No prior booking on record. Gate guard denies entry and asks bus to wait. After 12-minute delay, booking confirmed in a different system — entry granted. Group of 22 students and 3 teachers enter on foot with escort.

Parking lot B. A green motorcycle parks in a fire lane marker. Rider (male, courier company jacket) dismounts and walks toward main building. Guard follows up — rider directed back to authorized visitor bay. Complies without incident.

North fence exterior. A dog (medium-sized, stray) is digging near the base of the recently repaired fence panel. No immediate threat but noted in case it undermines the repair. Groundskeeper notified to check in the morning.
Loading dock. Packaging materials delivery completed. Truck departs. Bay 2 sealed. Dock officer begins end-of-afternoon inventory check on clipboard. Routine.
Rooftop. A pigeon nesting attempt observed in the northwest corner behind a duct cover. Nest material (twigs, plastic shreds) being gathered. Pest control to be notified. No security concern.
Rooftop. Clear and unoccupied. Late-afternoon sun causing glare on northwest section of camera. Lens auto-compensates. No anomalies.

South corridor. A large potted plant on the corridor floor is knocked over by a door swinging open — the plant pot shatters. Soil scattered on floor. The employee who caused it immediately reports to facilities via phone. Cleaning crew responds within 5 minutes.
South corridor. Student tour group passes through south corridor accompanied by corporate relations officer. Students stop to look at wall-mounted display panels. Orderly group, no issues.

South corridor. An individual in civilian clothing (male, 30-35 years, carrying a backpack) is observed walking against pedestrian flow and appears unfamiliar with the corridor layout. Guard approaches. Individual is a new employee on their first day, slightly lost. Directed to floor 2 HR desk.

Rear service gate. A large flatbed truck (RJ-14-**-5592) arrives unannounced with a load of construction scaffolding. Driver claims it is for upcoming external building repairs. Guard cannot verify on current schedule. Facilities manager confirms via phone that delivery is authorized but arrived 2 days early. Truck redirected to a temporary staging area outside the perimeter and rescheduled.

Rear service gate. A private car (KA-41-**-8841) parks outside rear gate. A male occupant exits and photographs the facility exterior walls and gate mechanism using a DSLR camera. Security personnel approach and request he cease photography. Individual claims to be an architecture student. ID noted; photography policy explained; individual departs.

Stairwell B, floor 2. A fire safety inspection sticker on one of the extinguishers is noted to be expired — visible during guard patrol. Maintenance ticket raised via radio. Extinguisher flagged with a caution tag until serviced.

Stairwell B, floor 3. Two male employees caught smoking in the stairwell near the top landing — confirmed by visible smoke plume. Fire sensor triggered. Security and facilities respond. Both employees escorted to HR. Stairwell ventilated. Incident documented.

Main gate. A large chartered coach (MH-09-**-2200) arrives to collect factory tour participants. Driver presents collection authorization. Gate opens for coach to pull into drop-off bay. Tour group of approximately 35 individuals boards the coach in an orderly manner. Coach departs after 9 minutes. Gate closed.
Main gate. Student tour group departs. Escort confirms headcount: 22 students, 3 teachers — all accounted for. Bus departs. Gate returns to normal pedestrian access mode.

Parking lot B. A suspicious dark-colored sedan (KA-07-**-0044) drives slowly through the entire parking lot twice — once clockwise and once counter-clockwise — without stopping or parking. Driver does not exit. Vehicle eventually leaves via main entrance. Behavior logged as suspicious loitering by vehicle. Partial plate recorded.

Parking lot B. End-of-day exodus begins. Steady stream of vehicles departing over 45-minute window. A minor fender-bender occurs between a silver hatchback and a white sedan reversing simultaneously from adjacent bays. Both drivers exchange information. No injuries. Security guard documents incident.

North fence. Two employees (male, both in high-vis) seen standing near fence panel 3 on the inside, leaning against the fence while on a break, eating and talking. No security concern. Guard confirms they are authorized personnel on a break.

North fence. A courier drone (company-marked DHL unit) descends toward the facility from the north. It lands briefly outside the fence and a small parcel is left near panel 6 — apparently a delivery attempt to the wrong address. Security retrieves parcel, confirms no risk, contacts courier company. Parcel redirected.
North fence. All clear. Evening light beginning. Groundskeeper has completed work and departed. No personnel near fence.

Loading dock. End of afternoon shift. The dock supervisor (male) conducts a full close-out inspection of all bays. Each bay door tested — all confirmed secure. CCTV coverage confirmed at all dock angles via radio with control room. Clean-up crew finishes sweeping dock floor. Shift ends without incident.
Loading dock. Dock shift handover at 17:45. Evening crew of 2 workers arrives. Dock doors all sealed. One truck (MH-48-**-3321) scheduled for 19:00 late delivery. Evening crew briefed accordingly.
Rooftop. Setting sun creating long shadows across rooftop surface. Both HVAC units cycling normally. Hatch confirmed locked. No personnel.

South corridor. Traffic dropping significantly. Remaining staff members heading out. One individual (male) re-enters the building from the south door at 18:10 after briefly stepping outside — badge scan logged correctly.

Rear service gate. Evening handover at rear gate. Outgoing guard briefs incoming guard on the suspicious motorcycle logged earlier and the scheduled morning deliveries. Logbook signed. Gate confirmed secure by both officers before handover completed.
Rear service gate. Evening security officer begins duty at rear gate. Signs in on digital log. Performs initial perimeter check. Gate padlock inspected and confirmed secure.

Stairwell B, floor 3. A maintenance worker (male, hard hat, tool belt) accesses the roof maintenance area via floor 3 stairwell hatch to check on a reported water leak. Spends 8 minutes above, descends, and reports findings to facilities coordinator waiting on the landing. No immediate risk identified; repair scheduled.
Stairwell B. Foot traffic now minimal. A single male employee (IT department shirt) ascends to floor 3, apparently working late. Badge scan normal.
Main gate. Evening guard takeover completed. Visitor log reviewed and cleared. All visitor badges accounted for. Gate reverts to night mode — pedestrian wicket only, vehicle gate locked.
Main gate. Pre-dawn. Gate arm in locked night position. Perimeter lights active. No vehicles or pedestrians. Control room confirms all gate sensors online. Quiet period documented.
Parking lot B. Approximately 8 vehicles remaining — long-term shift workers and late-stay staff. Lot lighting activates automatically at dusk. No anomalies.
Parking lot B. Dawn — lot completely empty. Automatic lighting begins to dim as natural light increases. Dew visible on parked barrier posts. Lot clear, no anomalies.

North fence. Twilight. A teenage boy attempts to climb the fence at panel 4, apparently trying to retrieve a football that has gone over. He succeeds in pulling the ball back through the mesh from outside without fully breaching the perimeter. Guard approaches from inside, warns him and sends him on his way. Documented as minor fence interaction.

Loading dock. Late delivery truck (MH-48-RT-3321) arrives at 19:27, 2 minutes ahead of schedule. Driver (male) presents manifest. Dock bay 3 opened. Three workers begin offloading palletized goods under dock lighting.

Rooftop. Low-light mode transitions to full IR as darkness sets in. Pan-tilt sweep conducted by control room at top of hour. All rooftop surfaces clear. No access to hatch. Perimeter lights reflected off flat bitumen surface — all normal.
Rooftop at dusk. Rooftop lights activate. Camera switches to low-light mode. No personnel detected. Hatch secured.
South corridor. Evening cleaning crew arrives — 2 individuals in blue uniforms with company-contracted cleaning company logo. Both verified against staff roster. Begin work in reception area.

Rear service gate. A three-wheeled cargo vehicle (auto-rickshaw type, no visible plate) pulls up to rear gate and driver asks the guard about a supposed pickup. No record of any such pickup in the evening schedule. Driver is turned away. Vehicle departs. Incident logged as potentially misrouted third-party courier.

Rear service gate. A black motorcycle (partial plate: AP-28-**) parks outside rear gate. Rider (helmeted) dismounts and appears to photograph the gate intercom and keypad area over approximately 3 minutes before departing. Classified as suspicious reconnaissance activity. Incident report filed.

Stairwell B, floor 2. A fire safety inspection sticker on one of the extinguishers is noted to be expired — visible during guard patrol. Maintenance ticket raised via radio. Extinguisher flagged with a caution tag until serviced.
Stairwell B, floor 1. The late-working IT employee descends stairwell. Badge scan logged at exit door. Departs building through south door.

Main gate. A group of four individuals (3 male, 1 female) approaches the pedestrian gate on foot. They appear to be in a celebratory mood — laughing loudly, one carrying a bottle. They attempt to gain entry claiming to visit a friend who works inside. Night guard denies entry per after-hours policy. The group lingers for about 5 minutes, then departs peacefully. Incident logged.

Parking lot B. A single vehicle remains in a remote bay long past normal hours. Security runs plate check — registered to an employee on record. Employee contacted via phone; confirms they took a taxi home due to a medical appointment and will retrieve the car tomorrow. Vehicle flagged in log for overnight continuity.

North fence, IR mode. Security rover unit (electric buggy) passes along the inner perimeter road. Officer visible, conducting mobile patrol. Slows at panel 9 repair site, shines torch — repair intact. Continues north along inner perimeter road.

North fence, IR mode. A lone male figure approaches the fence from outside at panel 12. He crouches low and appears to inspect the base of the fence, possibly looking for a gap or weakness. He remains in position for nearly 4 minutes before a vehicle passes on the road behind him, at which point he stands and walks away briskly. High-priority alert raised. Night patrols increased to 30-minute intervals.

Loading dock. A dock crew member discovers a cellphone left behind inside one of the empty delivery cages from the last truck. The phone is handed in to the guard post and logged as lost property. Driver of the truck contacted via manifest phone number.

Loading dock. Late delivery completed at 21:10. Truck departs. Dock bay 3 sealed and locked. Evening dock team begins closing procedure. Inventory tallied. No discrepancies. Dock lights reduced to low-power mode.
Rooftop. IR mode active. All clear. Wind gusting slightly. No access through hatch or via any other route detected.

Rooftop, late night. IR mode. Camera detects a dim light source near HVAC unit 2 — upon investigation via pan-tilt, it appears to be reflected moonlight on the metallic casing. No personnel present. False detection resolved.

South corridor. Cleaning crew continues work — now on floor 1 offices. One cleaner (male) enters an unoccupied office, cleans and exits within 4 minutes. No items appear to have been disturbed. Routine.
South corridor. All internal lights on minimum after-hours mode. Cleaning crew completed and gone. Corridor empty. Access door sensor active on all entry points. No motion detected.

Rear service gate. A physical altercation occurs just outside the rear gate between two males (not employees — both in civilian clothing). Punches exchanged. Guard calls police via facility radio and activates external alarm. Neither party attempts to breach the gate. Police arrive in 11 minutes. Both individuals detained. Footage archived for police evidence submission.
Rear service gate. All clear. Gate secured. Evening guard stationary at post, visible inside guard booth. Monitor showing multi-camera view.

Stairwell B, floor 1. During morning rush, a tailgating attempt is detected — an unrecognized individual in casual clothes follows closely behind a badged employee. System flags badge gap anomaly. Guard intercepts — individual is a new contractor who has not yet been issued a temporary badge. Escorted to reception for badge issuance.

Stairwell B. Late evening. Only night-shift security and cleaning staff remain in the building. Stairwell empty. All access points armed. Emergency lighting tested by guard during routine patrol — all lights functional. Logged as green.
Main gate. Vehicle (DL-01-**-9934) attempts to exit via entry lane — wrong direction. Guard stops vehicle and redirects to exit lane. Driver complies. No confrontation.

Main gate. Night mode confirmed. A pedestrian (male, hooded jacket) approaches gate intercom and presses call button. Guard responds. Individual claims to have left personal item inside. Guard asks for ID; individual cannot produce valid ID. Access denied. Individual leaves after brief verbal exchange. Incident logged.

Parking lot B. A car with engine running is stationary for over 10 minutes — occupant apparently on phone. Guard checks briefly; occupant (female) explains she is waiting for a colleague. Colleague arrives at 21:02, both depart together.
Parking lot B. Only 1 vehicle remaining — confirmed as belonging to the overnight security supervisor via registration log. Lot otherwise empty. All lights functioning.
North fence. Full night. Camera in IR mode. No personnel on either side of fence. Wind moderate; tree noise continues generating minor sensor interference. No genuine detections.
North fence. IR camera. Two foxes detected trotting along exterior fence base. No human activity. Fence sensors quiet after earlier adjustment.
Loading dock. Evening. Dock bay 1 repair completed by maintenance at 18:00. Dock supervisor signs off the work order. Bay 1 reinstated as operational. Evening crew briefed on restored capacity.
Loading dock. All dock bays confirmed sealed. Dock office locked. Evening dock team has signed out. Area quiet. Security camera coverage confirmed via control room test pan.

Rooftop. A facilities supervisor (female, white hard hat) performs a post-rain inspection following the previous day's heavy showers. Checks roof membrane, drains, and flashings. Photographs damage to one section of silicone sealant around HVAC unit 2 base. Work order raised. Departs after 12 minutes.
Rooftop. IR mode. Camera detects a large bird (likely an owl) perched on HVAC unit 1 casing. No human activity. Rooftop access hatch confirmed secured.
South corridor. Cleaning crew completes work on floor 1. Both members sign out at the south door. Door locks behind them on electronic latch. Corridor empty.
Rear service gate. IR mode. Gate fully secured. No activity detected for the past 45 minutes. Guard in booth visible on camera, seated, monitoring CCTV feed. Uneventful early morning period.
Rear service gate. IR mode. A cat sits on top of the gate post, observing the empty road. Motion sensor triggered. Guard reviews remotely and logs as animal false positive. No action required.

Rear service gate. Night guard doing hourly walk. Checks gate padlock and chain. Also checks perimeter light nearest rear gate — one bulb has failed. Reports to maintenance via radio. All else secure.

Stairwell B, floor 1. IR mode. Motion detected at ground floor stairwell door — the door opens slightly and then closes without anyone passing through. Guard reviews footage: a draft from a nearby HVAC vent caused the door to shift. Verified as false trigger via manual check. Door latch adjusted.

Stairwell B, floor 1. IR mode. A spider web across the corner of the camera lens is intermittently triggering motion detection false positives throughout the night. Logged for cleaning crew attention on the morning shift. Manually overridden in motion detection settings temporarily.
Stairwell B. All floors dark, no motion. End-of-day confirmed quiet. Security system armed at all stairwell doors. No anomalies through entire PM period.

Parking lot B. Overnight. Lone security vehicle (white SUV, facility livery) conducts a slow drive-through patrol of the lot. Officer visible inside vehicle, scanning with spotlight. Vehicle completes circuit and exits via access road. All clear.

Loading dock. Pre-shift inspection by dock supervisor. All bays checked — one dock plate is slightly misaligned on bay 1. Work order placed. Bay 1 marked out of service until repaired. Bays 2 and 3 available for the morning deliveries.

North fence, IR mode. Late night. Sensor detects movement at panel 3. PTZ camera zooms — confirmed as a small animal (likely a jackal or large fox) running along the outer fence line. No human activity. Motion log annotated: wildlife detection.

Main gate. Pre-dawn. First pedestrian entry of day — male in factory overalls, safety boots, hard hat clipped to belt. Swipes access card. Gate logs valid entry. He signs the physical paper log as required by site policy before proceeding.
